_meta.method: Knowledge + two web searches (H-1B status, German Blue Card 2026 thresholds); other visa routes cited from official portal landing pages listed in sources but NOT individually re-fetched this session - verify thresholds before relying on them.
_meta.tiers: UK/Ireland/Switzerland/Nordics are tier 'ok' (per brief) but still in the europe track; 'tier' is a preference weight, 'track' is the matching bucket.
_meta.suggested_priority: india > singapore > uae > europe > other_ok > remote_global > regional > us_optional; excluded/other_region/placeholder/unclassified are not alerts.
_meta.us_decision: United States is tier 'ok' with high_volume_hard_visa=true in its own track 'us_optional', not in other_ok. Trade-off: ~56% of sampled postings are US but H-1B is a lottery (wage-weighted selection from FY2027) and a USD 100k payment applies to certain new petitions (Proclamation of Sept 2025; confirm current status on USCIS). Default: show only if sponsorship/relocation is stated.

India.notes: Include states (karnataka etc.) because some feeds omit the city. 'Pan India', 'Anywhere in India', 'India (Remote)' and 'Remote - India' all contain the token india. ', IN' needs a special rule (Indiana).

Singapore.visa_route: Employment Pass (EP) with COMPASS points framework; Tech.Pass for senior talent; ONE Pass for top earners.
Singapore.notes: City-state: the country word is the city.

United Arab Emirates.visa_route: Employer-sponsored work visa/residence; 10-year Golden Visa for skilled professionals (incl. AI/tech specialists), Green Visa for skilled workers; 'Blue Visa' etc.
United Arab Emirates.notes: Tax-free salaries; very high posting volume. Watch for scam-prone recruiter spam but ATS-direct postings are fine.

Netherlands.visa_route: Highly Skilled Migrant (kennismigrant) permit via an IND-recognised sponsor; 30% ruling tax benefit (now phased down); EU Blue Card also possible.
Netherlands.notes: Recognised-sponsor requirement is easy to check on the IND public register.

Germany.visa_route: EU Blue Card (2026 salary floors ~EUR 50,700 standard / ~EUR 45,934 for shortage occupations incl. IT); Skilled Worker residence permit; Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte) for job search.
Germany.notes: ISO-2 'DE' collides with Delaware: never match ', DE' on its own.

France.visa_route: Talent Passport (Passeport Talent) - EU Blue Card or 'Salarié qualifié'/'Salarié en mission' categories; French Tech Visa for employees of recognised startups.
France.notes: Paris is the dominant AI hub (many labs). 'Paris' collides with Paris, TX.

Spain.visa_route: Highly Qualified Professional residence (Ley 14/2013, 'Unidad de Grandes Empresas'/UGE), EU Blue Card; Digital Nomad visa for remote workers.
Spain.notes: 'Valencia' collides with Valencia, CA; 'ES' ISO-2 is fine only as trailing country code.

Portugal.visa_route: Work visa for highly qualified activity / EU Blue Card; Tech Visa for certified tech employers; D8 Digital Nomad visa.
Portugal.notes: Strong volume of English-language tech jobs in Lisbon/Porto.

Italy.visa_route: Work permit under annual 'decreto flussi' quota; EU Blue Card for highly skilled; Digital Nomad visa.
Italy.notes: ISO-2 'IT' is a common English word: only match ', IT' as trailing code, never bare. 'Milan', 'Rome', 'Naples' collide with US towns.

Belgium.visa_route: Single permit (regional) for highly skilled workers / EU Blue Card (Brussels, Flanders, Wallonia).

Austria.visa_route: Red-White-Red Card (very skilled / shortage occupation) and EU Blue Card.
Austria.notes: 'Vienna' collides with Vienna, VA. ISO-3 'AUT' is fine only trailing.

Luxembourg.visa_route: EU Blue Card / highly qualified worker authorisation.
Luxembourg.notes: Country and capital share the name.

Ireland.visa_route: Critical Skills Employment Permit (ICT/AI roles on the Critical Skills list; 2-year path to Stamp 4).
Ireland.notes: Brief lists Ireland as 'ok'; still mapped to europe track. 'Dublin' collides with Dublin, OH/CA. Do NOT match 'northern ireland' as Republic (it is UK) - it matches UK first anyway.

United Kingdom.visa_route: Skilled Worker visa (employer licensed sponsor, ~GBP 41,700 general threshold since Apr 2025 plus occupation rules); Global Talent visa for AI leaders; Graduate route not applicable.
United Kingdom.notes: Skilled Worker rules tightened 2025; 'London' collides with London, ON; 'Cambridge' with Cambridge, MA. ISO-2 for UK is GB but postings use UK.

Switzerland.visa_route: Non-EU work permit (B/L) with annual quota; highly qualified specialists only, employer must prove no EU candidate.
Switzerland.notes: Quota for third-country nationals is tight, but salaries are the highest in Europe.

Sweden.visa_route: Work permit with employer offer meeting salary threshold (80% of median); EU Blue Card.
Sweden.notes: Nordic - listed 'ok' per brief; europe track.

Denmark.visa_route: Pay Limit Scheme / Positive List for highly skilled; Fast-Track scheme via certified companies; EU Blue Card.

Finland.visa_route: Residence permit for an employed person (specialist); EU Blue Card.

Norway.visa_route: Skilled worker residence permit (UDI) with salary requirement.
Norway.notes: ISO-2 'NO' collides with word 'no': never match.

Iceland.visa_route: Residence permit for specialists; EEA labour market test.

Poland.visa_route: Work permit type A / EU Blue Card; Poland Business Harbour (tech visa).

Czech Republic.visa_route: Employee Card; EU Blue Card; Czech tech talent scheme (Welcome Package).

Slovakia.visa_route: Blue Card / temporary residence for employment.

Hungary.notes: Guest-worker regime restricted; Blue Card is the practical route.

Greece.visa_route: Work permit / EU Blue Card; Digital Nomad visa.

Croatia.visa_route: Residence & work permit / EU Blue Card; Digital Nomad permit.

Estonia.visa_route: Employment registration + D-visa; e-Residency not a work route; Startup visa.

Lithuania.visa_route: Temporary residence for work / EU Blue Card; Startup visa.

Malta.visa_route: Single permit / Key Employee Initiative / EU Blue Card.

Cyprus.visa_route: Employment permit (Aliens and Immigration) / Blue Card.
Cyprus.notes: Only Republic of Cyprus; occupied north is not valid.

Serbia.visa_route: Work permit + temporary residence; relatively easy for IT.

Canada.visa_route: Express Entry (CRS points; Federal Skilled Worker/CEC) and Global Talent Stream (2-week work permit for tech employers).
Canada.notes: ISO-2 'CA' collides with California: never match bare ', CA'. 'ON' is Ontario but also a word.

Australia.visa_route: Skills in Demand visa (subclass 482; Specialist Skills pathway for high earners); Global Talent visa (subclass 858).
Australia.notes: 'Melbourne' collides with Melbourne, FL; 'Perth' with other minor.

New Zealand.visa_route: Accredited Employer Work Visa (AEWV) with median-wage rule.

Japan.visa_route: Highly Skilled Professional (points-based, fast PR); Engineer/Specialist in Humanities visa; J-Skip/J-Find.

South Korea.visa_route: E-7 Specialty Occupation visa; Top-Tier visa for elite talent; F-2-7 points visa.
South Korea.notes: Plain 'korea' maps here only; 'north korea' is excluded first.

Hong Kong.visa_route: General Employment Policy (GEP); Top Talent Pass Scheme (TTPS).
Hong Kong.notes: Borderline (political/regulatory risk) - kept as ok because visa route is straightforward and market is a regional finance/AI hub.

Taiwan.visa_route: Employment Gold Card (4-in-1 work/residence permit) for professionals.

Qatar.visa_route: Employer-sponsored work permit + residence permit (RP); tech roles concentrated in Doha.

Saudi Arabia.visa_route: Iqama via employer (Qiwa) / Premium Residency; heavy push for AI (HUMAIN, SDAIA).
Saudi Arabia.notes: Borderline - see borderline_decisions; kept as ok. Alias 'sa' NOT used (collides with South Africa/Australia).

Malaysia.visa_route: Employment Pass (EP, category I/II) / DE Rantau nomad pass.

Thailand.visa_route: Non-B visa + work permit; LTR (Long-Term Resident) visa for skilled professionals; Smart visa.

Vietnam.visa_route: Work permit via employer (requires degree + 3 yrs exp).

Indonesia.visa_route: KITAS work stay permit (employer-sponsored); Golden Visa for investors/talent.
Indonesia.notes: ISO-2 'ID' collides with Idaho and the word 'id'.

South Africa.visa_route: Critical Skills Work Visa (list includes some IT roles) / General Work Visa.
South Africa.notes: Borderline: high crime rate but lawful route and genuine tech hub. Low priority.

Brazil.visa_route: VITEM V work visa (employer-sponsored); Digital Nomad visa.
Brazil.notes: Low priority: most roles are Portuguese-language local hire. Amazon feed writes BRA.

Mexico.visa_route: Temporary resident with work permit via employer (INM).
Mexico.notes: Low priority; security varies by state.

Colombia.notes: ISO-2 'CO' collides with Colorado; ISO-3 'COL' trailing only.

United States.visa_route: H-1B (annual lottery; weighted-by-wage selection from FY2027; USD 100,000 payment on certain new petitions per Sept-2025 proclamation - verify current status), O-1 (extraordinary ability), L-1 intra-company transfer after 1 yr abroad.
United States.notes: High volume, hard visa. Flagged rather than hidden. Default recommendation: do NOT include in the main intl track; offer as a separate opt-in 'us_optional' bucket and show only if posting mentions sponsorship/relocation (visa_flag == yes) or role is an L-1/O-1 fit.

Uruguay.visa_route: Residence with work contract; digital nomad.

remote_rules.caveat: Country wins over the word remote. 'Remote - India' -> india.

remote_rules.pattern: remote - us | remote (us) | us only | usa only | remote, <US state code>
remote_rules.caveat: Must NOT match remote_global. Also catches 'Remote - CA/TX/NY' - 2-letter state after a dash.

remote_rules.pattern: worldwide | anywhere | global | distributed | work from home | 'Remote' alone | 'Remote International'
remote_rules.caveat: Keep only when job.kind == 'agg' as today, or require a visa_flag/relocation or eligibility text because many 'Remote' ATS postings are US/EU-timezone restricted. 'Anywhere in India' is NOT global; it contains 'india'. 'Anywhere' also appears in 'Ukraine Anywhere' - excluded check runs first.

remote_rules.pattern: emea | europe | european | eu | eea | dach | nordics | benelux | scandinavia | cee | eastern europe
remote_rules.caveat: EMEA also includes Middle East and Africa. Treat as europe (+ uae for Gulf). 'Home based - EMEA' is Europe+ME+Africa so lower confidence.
Region includes excluded countries; accept at region level only.

remote_rules.pattern: apac | apj | asia pacific | asia | south asia | southeast asia
remote_rules.caveat: APAC includes India and Singapore but also China, Australia; flag as 'regional' for review, treat like remote track (agg only).

remote_rules.pattern: north america | namer | americas | amer | latam | latin america | us and canada
remote_rules.caveat: Not a target. 'US and Canada' still hits Canada token if written 'Canada'.

remote_rules.pattern: hybrid | in-office | onsite | on-site | multiple locations | n locations | various | blank
remote_rules.caveat: Not enough information; do not drop silently - re-check against description or company HQ. 4.3% of sampled rows.

remote_rules.pattern: multi-location strings separated by | ; / or newline
remote_rules.caveat: Split first, classify each segment, priority india > singapore > uae > europe > other_ok > remote_global > regional > us_optional > excluded.

special_rules.rule: Case-sensitive: raw trailing r',\s*IN\s*$' -> India only if segment has no US signal and no Indiana city (indianapolis, fort wayne, west lafayette, bloomington). Never match bare 'in' (English word).
Match on original-case text: r'\bUS\b|\bU\.S\.|\bUSA\b' plus 'united states'. Never lowercase before this test; 'us' is not a token.
Safe lowercase: r'\buk\b' -> United Kingdom. 'GB' only as trailing ', GB'.

Treat ', CA' / '- CA' as California (US state). Canada is matched via 'canada', 'CAN' (trailing ISO-3), provinces (Ontario, British Columbia, Alberta, Quebec) and cities. ISO-2 'CA' for Canada is never used.
DE is NOT a US-state signal. Germany is matched from 'germany', 'DEU', or German city tokens. Bare 'DE' alone is not matched (Wilmington, DE -> unclassified).

Only trailing ', XX' for: gb nl fr ie ch se dk pl pt es sg ae jp kr hk tw nz au br mx. Never: in ca de it be at is no id co ar pa il (collide with words/US states). 'IT' as in 'Remote - IT' must not map to Italy.

Match only as trailing segment after , - | / e.g. r'[,\-|/]\s*(ind|gbr|ita|nld|deu|fra|esp|irl|che|swe|dnk|fin|bel|aut|pol|prt|sgp|are|can|aus|bra|jpn|kor|...)\s*$'. Do NOT use '(est)' (timezone), and do NOT match 'fin','bel','aut','pol','col','nor','esp' as free words (use trailing-only).

special_rules.problem: US cities that share names with target cities
special_rules.rule: Tokens paris, valencia, birmingham, cambridge, manchester, dublin, vienna, athens, naples, rome, milan, london, melbourne, perth, oxford, bristol, belfast, glasgow, newcastle, vancouver, portland, columbus, santiago, victoria are 'ambiguous': they count only when the segment has no US signal (state code, state name, 'United States').

US signal = US/USA/U.S., 'united states', [,-] two-letter US state (excl IN, DE), full state name, DC/'Washington, D.C.', 'Bay Area'. When present, drop all city-level matches (not country-name matches) in that segment.
No token (state vs country). Untracked unless other signals.
'northern ireland' is UK; both are europe track so no practical impact.
'Remote (US)'/'Remote - US'/'US only' -> us_optional; 'Remote, Canada; Remote, United States' -> any matching segment wins (other_ok).
NFKD-strip accents before matching (São Paulo, München, Zürich, Kraków). Boundary = (?<![a-z0-9])token(?![a-z0-9]) so 'Bengaluru-VTP' and 'Bengaluru - BLR1' match.

special_rules.problem: Short/ambiguous tokens deliberately removed from tracks
special_rules.rule: kl, blr, bgc, sa, au, nl, sg, hk, nz, roc, us, gb, york, salem, kota, derby, warwick, georgia, america, nice, bath, reading, split, cork-as-word(ambiguous list).

track_intl contains ISO-3 'fin','bel','aut','pol' and 'uk','nice'-like risk; 'ncr' ok; 'rome','milan','valencia' collide with US towns; 'remote' in track_remote matches 'Remote - US'. Replace by tracks + segment logic.
Compute concrete tracks first; set 'excluded' only when nothing target-side matched, so 'Tel Aviv | London' stays europe, 'Israel' alone is dropped.
us_optional (high_volume_hard_visa) should be shown only if visa_flag == 'yes' or relocation text appears; otherwise drop (56% of sampled rows are US).

Regex escape bug: 'd.c.' in US list matched 'dach' (DACH -> US); escaped
Removed ISO-2 'it','be','at','is' and 'est' ISO-3 (Remote - IT, '(EST)' timezone -> Estonia)
Removed 'DE' from US-state codes ('Berlin, DE' was classified US)
With an explicit US signal (state code, 'United States'), all city-level matches are suppressed ('Vancouver, WA', 'Dublin, OH', 'Cambridge, MA')
Added 'other_region' class (Americas, NAMER, LATAM) so 'Remote-NAMER' is not remote_global
